name: TalkBank conversational ASR dataset
description: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems have achieved remarkable performance on widely used benchmarks such as LibriSpeech and Fleurs. However, these benchmarks do not adequately reflect the complexities of real-world conversational environments, where speech is often unstructured and contains disfluencies such as pauses, interruptions, and diverse accents. In this study, we introduce a multilingual conversational dataset, derived from TalkBank, consisting of unstructured phone conversation between adults. Our results show a significant performance drop across various state-of-the-art ASR models when tested in conversational settings. Furthermore, we observe a correlation between Word Error Rate and the presence of speech disfluencies, highlighting the critical need for more realistic, conversational ASR benchmarks.
reputation: An emerging conversational ASR benchmark highlighting real-world disfluencies; currently of growing but limited adoption in the ASR community.
notes: Conversational, disfluent speech leads to substantially higher WER than read-speech benchmarks; potential privacy/transcription-convention issues and risk of overlap with existing corpora; non-LLM benchmark focused on acoustic/transcription performance.
